counterfactual_missing_items: Serologic analysis for HIV-1/2, antinuclear antibody, and antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies: negative
Chromoblastomycosis would require septate muriform bodies, whereas the raw biopsy specifies pigmented yeasts without multiaxial septation
decisive_items: Fungal skin culture: black yeastlike colonies characteristic of Exophiala spinifera species
pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia, parakeratosis, dense dermal infiltrate of histiocytes, foamy histiocytes, neutrophils, and multinucleate giant cells along with pigmented hyphae
Infiltrate of foamy histiocytes and pigmented yeasts without multiaxial septation (Fontana-Masson)
response.rationale: C1 is the most complete raw-supported diagnosis because the culture names Exophiala spinifera and the histology adds pigmented hyphae and yeasts, uniting cause and morphology. R6 has the same disease but omits species specificity, so it is the close runner-up. R2 is undermined by absence of muriform body septation and by the culture identifying Exophiala spinifera; R1 is only an anatomical sign, not the underlying diagnosis.

rejected.why: Culture recovered Exophiala spinifera, and histology describes pigmented yeasts without multiaxial septation, whereas chromoblastomycosis requires septate muriform bodies.
Saddle nose deformity is a destructive regional sign, not a diagnosis, and it is not causally supported by the culture or histology-confirmed etiology.
